subject: L13 lint bug: 'mm Hg' (two words) is never parsed as a unit, so every ABG value fails unit_missing
body:
`naadi_api/authoring/lint.py` L13 rejects every arterial blood gas value written the way the lab table writes it.

Repro: a stem containing "PaCO2 62 mm Hg and PaO2 58 mm Hg" gives
`L13 error {'analyte': 'paco2', 'value': 62.0, 'why': 'unit_missing'}`.

Cause: `_NUMBER_UNIT`'s `unit` group is one token (`[A-Za-z%][A-Za-z0-9%]*(?:/...)*`), so it captures "mm"; `norm_unit("mm")` = "mm" is not in the ref units {"mmhg", "kpa"}, has no "/" and is not "%", so it is reset to "" → unit_missing. The table's own unit "mm Hg" (with a space, as the NBME table and every exam stem write it) can never match.

Suggested fix: let the unit group take an optional second word for this case, e.g. `(?P<unit>mm\s?Hg|cm\s?H2O|[A-Za-zµμ%][A-Za-zµμ%0-9]*(?:/[A-Za-zµμ0-9]+)*)`, plus a unit test with "PaO2 58 mm Hg".

Impact: 10 errors in cardio-resp (all ABG items in 09.03/09.06); any author with blood gases will hit it. I will not respell units to "mmHg" to dodge the linter unless you say so.
